newsitem.title: USA: USDA studying upping Russia GSM-102 credit line.
newsitem.headline: USDA studying upping Russia GSM-102 credit line.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Export Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said Wednesday USDA is mulling upping Russia's GSM-102 credit line after a report that the country may seek U.S. or Canadian wheat.
Russian Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun said Tuesday Russia would import up to three million tonnes of high-quality wheat in 1997.

"We've heard in general terms of their interest, we've had no official approach from Russia in this regard," Goldthwait said in a telephone interview with USDA Radio from the World Trade Organization meeting in Singapore.

"We do have a small GSM-102 credit guarantee line that is available for Russia that could be helpful in this regard. A good bit of it has been utilized already this fiscal year and we are currently studying the prospect of increasing it," he said.
Goldthwait pointed out that last year Russia's credit line was raised when needed.
